subject.title: Feature: Inject context window % into system prompt runtime section

question: Should OpenClaw expose passive context-window usage in the system-prompt Runtime line, and if so what freshness and display contract should it use?
rationale: The code path is identifiable, but this changes the per-turn prompt contract and overlaps with broader runtime self-context work, so automation should not choose the product semantics.

options.title: Approve bounded Runtime context metadata
options.body: Add a compact optional `context=<percent>` field below the cache boundary, with documented stale/unknown behavior and focused tests across prompt assembly and embedded/Codex surfaces.

options.title: Fold into runtime self-context design
options.body: Keep this issue open as a requirement for #89537 and avoid adding a separate Runtime field until the broader runtime context contract lands.

options.title: Keep explicit tools only
options.body: Decline passive prompt injection and document `/status` plus `session_status` as the supported way to retrieve current context usage.

recommendation.title: Approve bounded Runtime context metadata
recommendation.body: Add a compact optional `context=<percent>` field below the cache boundary, with documented stale/unknown behavior and focused tests across prompt assembly and embedded/Codex surfaces.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent runtime-context prompt/cache work makes this the closest current product-contract ownership signal for volatile prompt metadata.
